evidence: The Windows release path still holds and renames the exact cache root by handle. R03 additionally records every directory identity in the confirmed inventory, opens stable no-delete-share handles for the entire tree, and installs reversible same-user deny-add ACLs before the destructive rename.

After all namespace guards are installed, the complete inventory is recomputed. The deny-add ACLs then move with the exact cache tree and remain active across post-move validation, replacement-cache creation, audit commit, and physical cleanup, preventing canonical directories or substituted children from entering deletion authority.

On any pre-audit denial, rollback uses the held cache handle while ACL guards remain active, restores the exact cache path, restores original ACLs, preserves canonical paths and bytes, and records no success audit. After a successful audit, incomplete physical cleanup leaves a protected cleanup-pending tombstone that rejects later canonical insertion instead of risking deletion.

Windows adversarial tests now attack the exact pre-rename, post-move, post-validation, and post-audit boundaries. Root and child substitutions are denied; pre-audit requests return no cleared result or success audit; canonical and cache bytes remain at their exact paths; rollback restores ordinary cache write access; and no unsafe tombstone remains.

The post-audit case proves the staged tree remains protected until identity-bound cleanup. Because the attempted external namespace mutation is denied and does not alter the operation, the valid clear completes with exact canonical bytes and one truthful audit.

A forced cleanup interruption proves the cleanup-pending tombstone retains deny-add protection and rejects a subsequent attempt to move canonical config beneath it. The full 43-test security suite, strict contract suite, desktop verifier, and 140-file quality checks pass.
The strict descendant changes only the privacy cache-clear implementation and its acceptance-bound security tests beyond immutable R02 evidence/review records and generated workflow projections.

No provider, telemetry, retention, public route, portable schema, database profile, dependency, UI reference, or unrelated capability changed. Existing consent, session, audit redaction, deletion disclosure, and approved UI behavior remain green.

Both prior high-severity finding IDs are replayed for independent closure. Protected-database selection and broader migration, performance, packaging, and cross-capability qualification remain assigned to T04, slice review, checkpoints, and W1 exit.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: CAP-02.S04.T03-R01-F01 showed that path inventory without a stable root handle could redirect destructive authority; CAP-02.S04.T03-R02-F01 showed that root binding alone still allowed child namespace insertion into the staged tree and could defeat rollback. R03 therefore expands coverage to per-directory identity and reversible deny-add ACL installation, post-install re-inventory, pre-rename/root substitution, post-move child insertion, post-validation insertion, post-audit insertion, rollback ACL restoration, audit ordering, protected cleanup-pending quarantine, full local security, strict privacy contracts, the complete desktop verifier, governed Python quality, unchanged UI-reference lineage, and canonical workflow integrity. Dependency scanning, SQLCipher/database protection, performance, packaging, and full cross-capability qualification remain deferred because this remediation changes no dependency, database engine, packaging input, UI reference, or performance contract and those surfaces belong to T04, CAP-02.S04 review, checkpoints, and W1 exit.

reviewerDisposition.rootCauseAnalysis: R01 treated inventory equality plus path-based rename as sufficient destructive authority, overlooking root replacement. R02 corrected the root handoff with a stable Windows handle but still assumed the staged tree's child namespace remained unchanged, so an inserted canonical directory could make rollback fail. R03 makes namespace immutability explicit: it binds every confirmed directory identity, installs reversible deny-add ACLs under held handles before rename, revalidates the fully protected tree, carries those ACLs through audit and cleanup, restores them on rollback, and retains them on cleanup-pending quarantine.
